text:
Maya: thinking out loud - proposal to replace our scattered pin/fallback heuristics with a single deterministic resolver function in the control plane. goal: one place to reason about why a variant was chosen.

Oliver: would this supplant the multi-step routing (pin -> affinity -> fallback) we currently have?

Maya: yes. high level: hierarchy still exists (HARD_PIN/ANCHOR short-circuit), but when none apply we run the resolver which scores candidates and picks the highest.

Rik: ok but make it strictly deterministic. floating point scores and unstable sorts bite us in canaries. prefer integer math and explicit tie-break keys.

Priya: agree. suggest score = health_score*100 + hint_weight - staleness_penalty. then final sort key = (score, canonical_variant_id, epoch).

Maya: that'll be resolver_v1 behavior. we'll include resolver_version in rollout metadata so decisions are auditable and replayable.

Jon: how do anchors/pins fit? if a tenant sets an anchor we should never override it with resolver logic. anchors stay top priority.

Maya: exactly. order is: HARD_PIN -> ANCHOR -> RESOLVER -> GLOBAL_FALLBACK. resolver only runs when higher levels don't resolve a choice.

Asha: ops concern: older control planes may not understand a new resolver_profile blob. migration?

Maya: plan: metadata carries resolver_version (string) and an optional resolver_profile (small kv list). resolver_profile must be additive and optional; default semantics for each version are documented. include min_control_plane_version if profile needs it.

Priya: need TTL for ephemeral hints or signals (e.g., recent latency). add hint_ttl_s and ensure the resolver ignores expired hints. example snippet in text: ```json
{"resolver_version":"v2","resolver_profile":["latency_hint:30"],"hint_ttl_s":"300","staleness_penalty":"10"}```

Rik: keep profile tiny. also require that any client-visible behavior change include a compatibility flag and a migration window. add a test harness to replay old metadata across versions to assert determinism.

Oliver: we should also encode compatibility_level for variants (strong, weak). resolver prefers strong unless scoring pushes a weak variant higher. document what strong/weak imply (tokenizer/arch match vs best-effort).

Jon: tenant isolation: resolver should be tenant-scoped. different tenants can have different profiles and pins; resolver doesn't mix contexts.

Asha: observability: expose chosen_variant, resolver_version, score_components (small list), and reason in traces. make the reason human-friendly like "anchor" or "score:42+id:abc". keep size bounded.

deploy-bot: rollout-resolver/v2 queued -> staging (canary 3%) 2026-03-20T13:05:00Z. CI green.

Maya: i'll draft a follow-up RFC with: algorithm pseudocode, exact metadata fields (resolver_version, resolver_profile, hint_ttl_s, staleness_penalty, compatibility_level, min_control_plane_version), migration steps, and observability wire format. tagging @Oliver @Rik for review.

Oliver: happy to review.

Rik: will add deterministic replay unit tests and run historical fixtures.

Maya: thanks all, will post the doc here when ready. :wave:
